items.t: Horn works only some of the time (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 96V-088: dealers add a ground contact spring for the horn. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Ignition switch housing cracks (recall)
items.note: Free under recalls 00V-317 and 06V-403: dealers install a new ignition switch. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Rear seat belts may not lock (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 97V-115. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Tie rod end seals fail (recall)
items.job: Replace outer tie rod ends and align
items.note: Free under recall 99V-248 (and 00V-414): dealers replace the tie rods. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Oil sludge in the 1.8T engine
items.job: Drop oil pan, clean pickup screen and change oil
items.note: If the engine was damaged from low oil pressure, a replacement engine costs much more.

items.t: Ignition coil failures
items.job: Replace ignition coils and spark plugs
items.note: Price is for all four coils and plugs; one coil costs less. Basis: YourMechanic (no parts-plus-labor source found): about $494–$558 estimate for 2005–2007 1.8T/2.0T, national average $289.

items.t: Crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve and hoses fail
items.job: Replace PCV valve and breather hoses
items.note: Basis: YourMechanic (no parts-plus-labor source found): about $196–$309 for a 1.8T and $417–$770 for a 2.0T. Cost rises if several breather hoses are cracked.

items.t: Multitronic CVT failure on front-drive models
items.job: Replace Multitronic CVT with a rebuilt unit
items.note: Some cars are fixed with a control module repair or fluid service, which costs much less.

items.t: Fuel pump can quit and stall the engine (recall)
items.note: Free under recalls 06V-017 and 07V-375. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Xenon headlights dim over time (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 05V-096. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Camshaft lobe and cam follower wear
items.job: Replace high-pressure fuel pump cam follower
items.note: If the cam lobe is worn, replacing the camshaft and fuel pump costs much more.

items.t: Air bag control unit can corrode (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 16V-376: dealers replace the air bag control unit. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
items.note: Basis: RepairPal, $987–$1,232 total for the tensioner (no parts-plus-labor source found). Replacing the chain, guides and all tensioners took about 9 labor hours for one AudiWorld owner, and a chain that jumped can damage valves.

items.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leaks
items.job: Replace water pump and thermostat housing
items.note: Basis: YourMechanic (no parts-plus-labor source found): about $664–$971 estimate for 2010–2018 2.0T thermostat replacement, $734–$1,409 at shops and dealers. The 2.0T thermostat sits in the water pump housing.

items.t: Electric after-run coolant pump can overheat (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 18V-229 (after the 17V-002 software update): dealers replace the pump. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Passenger air bag may switch off (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 21V-874 (expands 19V-547): dealers replace the seat heater cable and heating mat or seat cover. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Rear trailing arm nut can crack (recall)
items.note: Free under recalls 21V-295 and 22V-034: dealers replace the lock nuts and check rear alignment. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Rear seat belts may unlock too early (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 21V-606: dealers replace the middle-rear belt as needed. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Rearview camera shows a blank screen (recall)
items.note: Free under recalls 21V-825, 22V-742 and 22V-806: dealers update the software or replace the infotainment unit. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Engine can stall from a faulty engine computer (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 22V-368: dealers replace the engine control unit. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture or inflate weakly (recalls)
items.job: Replace driver air bag inflator module
items.note: Free under recall 20V-056, 21V-470 or 22V-471: dealers replace the driver air bag inflator. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Whistle from the turbo at steady throttle
Low coolant message with the level actually correct
items.job: Replace coolant level sensor and test grille shutter

items.t: Gearbox warning with limp mode or no reverse
items.job: Diagnose transmission control module and reprogram
items.note: Cost rises a lot if the clutch pack or mechatronic unit turns out to be the cause.

items.t: Shudder or binding in tight turns on quattro models
items.job: Service rear axle clutch and update all-wheel-drive software

items.t: Will not start after sitting from a flat battery
items.job: Replace 12-volt battery, register it and test for drain

items.t: Driver air bag can fire from static electricity (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 97V-175: dealers add a ground wire to the driver air bag. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Weak brake assist in cold weather (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 99V-131. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.

items.t: Throttle may not return to idle after a backfire (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 98V-134. Check your VIN with an Audi dealer first.
